001package bank.model;
002
003import java.util.ArrayList;
004import java.util.List;
005
006/**
007 * ============================================================================
008 *  Bank.java
009 *  Owner: John (smartdude879@gmail.com)
010 * ============================================================================
011 *
012 *  REPRESENTS:
013 *      The top-level "bank" container — really just a list of all customers.
014 *      This is the object that gets serialized to and from bank.json.
015 *
016 *  WHY A WRAPPER CLASS:
017 *      Gson works best with a single root object. By wrapping the customer list
018 *      in a Bank, we can later add fields (next account number, bank name, etc.)
019 *      without breaking the JSON format.
020 * ============================================================================
021 */
022public class Bank {
023
024    /** Every customer the bank knows about. */
025    private List<Customer> customers = new ArrayList<>();
026
027    /** No-arg constructor required by Gson. */
028    public Bank() { }
029
030    /**
031     * Returns the live list of customers — mutations are persisted on save().
032     */
033    public List<Customer> getCustomers() {
034        if (customers == null) {
035            customers = new ArrayList<>();
036        }
037        return customers;
038    }
039}
